purpose.statement: Provide a deterministic, provider-neutral orchestration runtime that turns approved goals into accepted software through explicit modular engineering contracts, evidence, gates, and traceable lifecycle progression.

businessObjectives.statement: Make software-engineering progression reproducible and fail closed when required inputs, evidence, or approvals are invalid.
Allow best-in-class engineering capabilities to be replaced without changing canonical workflow semantics or generic Core.
Require scoped verification and evidence before work, changes, systems, or business outcomes advance.
Trace every approved business objective through requirements, design, planned work, implementation, verification, integration, and acceptance.
Prevent invalid, cyclic, incomplete, or impossible dependency plans from reaching assignment and execution.
Replace dependency-analysis capabilities without changing canonical semantics or generic Core.
Provide authoritative ordering sufficient for downstream systems to identify safely runnable work.

successMetrics.name: Deterministic progression
successMetrics.measure: Repeated Core-owned routing, validation, replay, and gate decisions for identical content-addressed inputs.
successMetrics.measurementMethod: Run positive, negative, drift, checkpoint, replay, and gate conformance suites.

successMetrics.name: Adapter-independent semantics
successMetrics.measure: Compatible adapter replacements requiring a product-specific behavioral branch in generic Core.
successMetrics.measurementMethod: Execute adapter replacement fixtures and scan generic Core for product identifiers.

successMetrics.name: Verified progression
successMetrics.measure: Lifecycle transitions occurring without the configured passing evidence and approval record.
successMetrics.measurementMethod: Audit module execution records, gate decisions, verification evidence, and acceptance receipts.

successMetrics.name: Lifecycle trace coverage
successMetrics.measure: Approved business objectives with a complete trace to implementation and passing verification evidence by BusinessAcceptance.
successMetrics.target: 100 percent or an explicit approved disposition.
successMetrics.measurementMethod: Run TraceabilityGraph coverage and orphan diagnostics at each lifecycle horizon.

successMetrics.name: Generic Core product branches
successMetrics.measure: WorkDependencyAnalysis, Spec Kit, or OpenSpec identifier branches in generic Core.
successMetrics.measurementMethod: Run static special-case scans and adapter-replacement conformance tests.

successMetrics.name: Unsafe runnable frontier
successMetrics.measure: Work items exposed as runnable while an authoritative predecessor remains incomplete.
successMetrics.measurementMethod: Derive runnable frontiers from approved DAG fixtures and predecessor completion state.

successMetrics.name: Invalid dependency progression
successMetrics.measure: Invalid endpoint, duplicate or self edge, cycle, unresolved missing dependency, or impossible ordering cases reaching an approved baseline.
successMetrics.measurementMethod: Run positive and negative WorkDependency Gate fixtures and inspect exact promotion receipts.

steps.action: Execute and verify each work item before integration.
steps.expectedOutcome: Only individually verified changes enter integration.

steps.action: Verify the integrated system and evaluate business acceptance.

userStories.need: Require evidence before work items, integrated changes, or business outcomes are accepted.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: Adapters receive only declared inputs and capability grants and cannot route workflow, approve artifacts, mutate TraceabilityGraph, or create undeclared Core behavior.
acceptanceCriteria.verification: Run prohibited-capability, hidden-context, graph-access, and Core-special-case fixtures for each adapter family.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: Every lifecycle handoff uses a schema-valid, immutable, content-addressed artifact with explicit lineage and no reliance on conversational memory.
acceptanceCriteria.verification: Audit every V1 module manifest, invocation, result contract, checkpoint, and downstream input binding.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: ArchitectureDiscovery runs only for an existing repository without a validated architecture baseline or current snapshot, and ContractGeneration runs only when approved interface intent requires formal contracts.
acceptanceCriteria.verification: Execute every eligible and ineligible state fixture and verify Core-owned route decisions and zero adapter calls on rejected routes.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: The approved project overview contains exactly RequirementsGathering, RequirementsGate, ArchitectureDiscovery, ArchitectureDesign, ArchitectureGate, ContractGeneration, WorkBreakdown, WorkDependencyAnalysis, SpecialistAssignment, WorkExecution, WorkItemVerification, ChangeIntegration, SystemVerification, and BusinessAcceptance in that order.
acceptanceCriteria.verification: Compare the ordered owner-approved inventory with the deterministic scope projection and fail on omission, addition, reordering, or conditionality drift.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: A configured gate prevents progression until exact candidate, policy, evidence, approval, and baseline-promotion requirements pass.
acceptanceCriteria.verification: Attempt progression with missing, stale, forged, rejected, and passing gate inputs at each implemented boundary.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: Changing the AI model or bounded implementation tool does not alter the canonical module sequence, artifact contracts, gates, or traceability vocabulary.
acceptanceCriteria.verification: Run compatible adapter substitutions and compare canonical outputs, validation, route, and graph contracts.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: Interrupted effectful executions resume only from exact validated checkpoints and do not repeat already checkpointed effects.
acceptanceCriteria.verification: Interrupt and replay each effectful execution profile and assert exact lineage with zero duplicate adapter calls.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: TraceabilityGraph can traverse each accepted business objective through requirements, architecture, contracts when applicable, planned work, changes, tests, evidence, integration, and acceptance while diagnosing missing links.
acceptanceCriteria.verification: Run forward and reverse lifecycle queries plus orphan, unscoped-work, and missing-evidence diagnostics at each implemented horizon.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: WorkItemVerification and SystemVerification record scoped passing evidence before ChangeIntegration and BusinessAcceptance respectively.
acceptanceCriteria.verification: Exercise passing and failing evidence packages and verify downstream progression remains blocked until the required proof passes.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: The bounded Spec Kit analyze capability acts only as a consistency and coverage reviewer after canonical proposal normalization and cannot add authoritative edges or approve the candidate.
acceptanceCriteria.verification: Return reviewer passes, warnings, proposed corrections, malformed outputs, and contradictions and verify that only Gate-owned policy can resolve blocking findings.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: Every ContextSlice declares its purpose, source artifact reference, source kind and version or commit, deterministic selector, extracted-content digest, and covered work-item or proposal references; undeclared adapter-selected context is forbidden.
acceptanceCriteria.verification: Reject missing relevance, overbroad selectors, unresolved source pointers, duplicate slices, uncovered references, and byte or version drift before any proposal effect.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: Trusted Core uses its pinned Graphology and Graphology-DAG implementation to reject self-dependencies and every directed cycle with a deterministic canonical cycle witness.
acceptanceCriteria.verification: Exercise self-loop, two-node, nested, disconnected, and insertion-order variants and compare canonical witnesses across replays.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: Exact inputs, adapter identity, configuration, grants, policy, and checkpoint state produce the same Core-owned route, validation, graph digest, diagnostics, and replay without reinvocation.
acceptanceCriteria.verification: Execute repeated and replayed runs and compare outputs and call counts.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: A candidate is bound to one exact WorkBreakdownBaseline and contains every baseline work-item ID exactly once with no additional IDs.
acceptanceCriteria.verification: Run exact-set fixtures for omitted, duplicated, and foreign IDs.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: Graphology and Graphology-DAG remain replaceable implementation libraries behind Core-owned canonical graph mechanics; their native serialization, traversal order, or diagnostic wording never becomes the DevRelay artifact contract.
acceptanceCriteria.verification: Feed equivalent insertion orders and library-native shapes and compare canonical node, edge, topological-order, cycle-witness, and diagnostic bytes.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: Every dependency hint receives exactly one evidence-backed disposition.
acceptanceCriteria.verification: Exercise accepted, rejected, replaced, duplicated, and omitted dispositions.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: Core constructs one complete immutable WorkBreakdownAnalysisSnapshot from the exact approved WorkBreakdownBaseline and admits only declared relevant ContextSlice entries whose source artifact version, content digest, or repository commit and extracted-content digest all verify before proposer entry.
acceptanceCriteria.verification: Mutate the baseline pointer, slice selector, source version, source digest, repository commit, or extracted-content digest and verify pre-proposer rejection with zero proposer calls.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: WorkDependencyGate rejects unresolved blocking missing-dependency findings from the exact native proposal, OPA decision set, consistency review, and Gate-owned semantic review.
acceptanceCriteria.verification: Use omitted-prerequisite fixtures and verify that proposer silence or a passing mechanical DAG cannot authorize promotion.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: The default proposer is a DevRelay-native structured proposer that consumes only the full analysis snapshot and declared context slices and returns the same provider-neutral DependencyProposal contract required from optional proposal adapters.
acceptanceCriteria.verification: Run native, Task Master, and OpenSpec proposal fixtures through the same schema, lineage, hint-disposition, provenance, and substitution suite.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: WorkDependencyAnalysis does not assign, estimate, schedule, execute, modify code, record completion, or collect implementation evidence.
acceptanceCriteria.verification: Inspect schemas, capabilities, effects, fixtures, and graph assertions for prohibited fields and effects.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: OPA evaluates a version-pinned policy bundle against one canonical JSON input document and returns a normalized decision set whose bundle digest, entrypoint, input digest, engine version, and raw result evidence are checkpoint-bound.
acceptanceCriteria.verification: Exercise allow, deny, undefined, malformed, stale-bundle, wrong-entrypoint, nondeterministic-input-order, and evaluation-failure fixtures.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: WorkDependencyGate rejects invalid endpoints, duplicate edges, contradictory evidence, OPA-denied relationships, unresolved reviewer findings, and other policy-forbidden ordering.
acceptanceCriteria.verification: Run one negative fixture per rejection and verify stable diagnostics and no promotion payload.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: The approved artifact provides predecessor relationships sufficient for a later scheduler to derive runnable work without mutable assignment or execution state.
acceptanceCriteria.verification: Derive frontiers for multiple completion states while the dependency artifact remains unchanged.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: The default native structured proposer and optional Task Master or OpenSpec proposal adapters may return only the canonical proposal contract; Spec Kit may return only consistency-review findings; none may route, validate Core mechanics, evaluate promotion policy, access TraceabilityGraph, or claim authority.
acceptanceCriteria.verification: Swap every proposer and reviewer binding, attempt prohibited outputs and graph operations, and scan generic routing Core for product identifiers.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: A trusted contributor derives only forward candidate dependency relationships; Core checkpoint-merges them and Gate approval activates separate authoritative scope without inverse or completion edges.
acceptanceCriteria.verification: Attempt adapter graph operations, then verify projection, merge proof, replay, retirement, and approved authority.

nonFunctionalRequirements.statement: Core-owned routing, validation, checkpoint replay, traceability projection, and gate preparation must be deterministic for exact inputs.
nonFunctionalRequirements.measure: Canonical route, result, diagnostic, update, and receipt digest equality.
nonFunctionalRequirements.target: 100 percent equality for deterministic Core-owned behavior.

nonFunctionalRequirements.statement: Canonical lifecycle contracts must remain independent of IDE, AI provider, model, operating host, and bounded external tool.
nonFunctionalRequirements.measure: Compatible host and adapter substitutions requiring canonical contract changes.

nonFunctionalRequirements.statement: Every accepted lifecycle assertion must retain exact artifact, contributor, execution, authority, and graph-version provenance.
nonFunctionalRequirements.measure: Accepted graph assertions lacking complete resolvable provenance.

nonFunctionalRequirements.statement: Routing, mechanical validation, canonical ordering, replay, and Gate commit preparation must be deterministic for exact inputs.
nonFunctionalRequirements.measure: Canonical output, diagnostic, route, and replay digest equality.
nonFunctionalRequirements.target: 100 percent equality for deterministic Core-owned behavior.

constraints.statement: Every stage must exchange canonical structured artifacts and cannot rely on conversational memory as authority.
constraints.rationale: Explicit artifacts make lifecycle state reproducible and verifiable.

constraints.statement: Producing modules cannot approve or promote their own candidates; configured gates own progression decisions.
constraints.rationale: Separate authority prevents production from becoming self-approval.

constraints.statement: V1 lifecycle scope is limited to the fourteen owner-approved components recorded in the project overview.
constraints.rationale: A closed inventory prevents silent V1 scope expansion.

constraints.statement: Canonical Core and module contracts cannot depend on one AI model, provider, IDE, or external engineering product.
constraints.rationale: The workflow owns engineering semantics; tools only perform bounded capabilities.

constraints.statement: WorkDependencyAnalysis is analysis and approval, not assignment, scheduling, or execution.
constraints.rationale: Separate lifecycle authority prevents planned ordering from becoming an execution claim.

constraints.statement: Canonical contracts and Core cannot depend on a model, Spec Kit, OpenSpec, or another analyzer product.
Traceability stores forward dependency assertions only and derives reverse traversal at query time.
constraints.rationale: One direction avoids duplicated inconsistent facts.

scope.statement: RequirementsGathering [module]: RequirementsGathering converts an explicit goal and project context into a canonical requirements candidate and deterministic ProjectOverview candidate.
RequirementsGate [gate]: RequirementsGate validates and approves one exact RequirementsBaseline and ProjectOverviewBaseline pair before architecture progression.
ArchitectureDiscovery [module; conditional]: ArchitectureDiscovery conditionally establishes a validated current-architecture snapshot for an existing repository that has no architecture baseline.
ArchitectureDesign [module]: ArchitectureDesign converts approved requirements into a new architecture candidate or a proposed architecture change.
ArchitectureGate [gate]: ArchitectureGate validates architectural fitness, evidence, and approval before establishing or updating the ArchitectureBaseline.

ContractGeneration [module; conditional]: ContractGeneration conditionally produces and validates API, schema, event, protocol, and other machine-readable interface contracts when the approved design requires them.
WorkBreakdown [module]: WorkBreakdown converts approved scope into a complete set of bounded, traceable, independently executable and verifiable work items without executing them.
WorkDependencyAnalysis [module]: WorkDependencyAnalysis validates authoritative ordering and dependencies between approved work items before assignment or execution.
SpecialistAssignment [module]: SpecialistAssignment selects a compatible human or implementation engine for each ready work item from explicit capability requirements and policy.
WorkExecution [module]: WorkExecution performs one authorized work item against exact inputs and returns bounded deliverables, changes, diagnostics, and evidence without owning acceptance.
WorkItemVerification [module]: WorkItemVerification checks each executed work item against its verification plan and required evidence before it can enter integration.
ChangeIntegration [module]: ChangeIntegration combines individually verified changes in dependency-safe order and records the exact integrated state.
SystemVerification [module]: SystemVerification validates the integrated system across functional, security, performance, operational, documentation, and other configured quality policies.
BusinessAcceptance [module]: BusinessAcceptance evaluates the verified system against approved business objectives, success metrics, scope, and acceptance criteria and records the final disposition.
Bounded replaceable analysis manifests and conformance fixtures.
Provider-neutral dependency analysis bound to exact WorkBreakdown and upstream context.
Dependency state, policy, hint-disposition, edge, finding, candidate, baseline, clarification, diagnostic, and Gate evidence artifacts.
Version-pinned relevant context slicing and pre-proposer coherence validation.
A separate Gate for graph mechanics, semantic policy, approval, and exact promotion.
Pinned OPA policy bundle evaluation and normalized decision evidence.
A bounded post-proposal consistency-review slot with Spec Kit as the V1 binding.
A trusted contributor and candidate-to-approved authority transition.

nonGoals.statement: Build another monolithic coding agent or AI-provider wrapper.
nonGoals.rationale: DevRelay standardizes deterministic engineering workflow rather than code generation.

nonGoals.statement: Treat model confidence, adapter output, chat history, or successful execution as implicit approval.
nonGoals.rationale: Only explicit validated gates and evidence authorize progression.

nonGoals.statement: Reimplement full upstream tools such as OpenSpec, Spec Kit, Structurizr, or MADR inside Core.
nonGoals.rationale: DevRelay invokes only bounded replaceable capabilities.

nonGoals.statement: Add lifecycle modules outside the approved V1 inventory without a new requirements change and overview baseline.
nonGoals.rationale: V1 scope must remain deliberate and auditable.

nonGoals.statement: Choose a specialist, model, agent, or human.
Introduce a distributed scheduler, agent framework, provider wrapper, or general control plane.
nonGoals.rationale: This release is an incremental module slice.

nonGoals.statement: Execute, implement, test, or verify a work item.
Persist schedules, estimates, capacity, or runtime execution waves.
nonGoals.rationale: Scheduling depends on changing runtime state.

terminology.definition: A lifecycle module invoked only when exact Core-owned state and approved policy satisfy its declared condition.
A separate validation and approval boundary that decides whether an exact candidate may become an approved baseline or progress downstream.
A provider-neutral lifecycle contract defining exact inputs, action, outputs, outcomes, evidence, and progression boundary.
The compact approved project-wide context deterministically projected from the paired RequirementsBaseline and explicitly supplied to downstream modules.
A Core-owned cross-cutting lifecycle index that records validated artifact relationships beside the module sequence without becoming a workflow stage.
The complete immutable projection of one exact approved WorkBreakdownBaseline used as the work-item universe for a single full dependency analysis.
A deterministic, relevance-declared extraction from one immutable version-pinned source artifact, supplied as explicit analyzer input with its own content digest.
A directed acyclic graph where each forward edge says one predecessor must complete before one successor may start.
The evidence-backed treatment of one non-authoritative WorkBreakdown dependency hint.
A dependency forbidden by exact domain, architecture, contract, repository, or policy evidence even when acyclic.
Work items whose authoritative predecessors are complete under current runtime state.

currentStatus.summary: The five WorkDependencyAnalysis boundary decisions are confirmed. The requirements change candidate is ready for Requirements Gate review before ArchitectureDesign.

assumptions.statement: ArchitectureDiscovery and ContractGeneration are conditional lifecycle modules rather than mandatory work for every project or change.
The fourteen lifecycle components in the approved scope are the complete DevRelay V1 inventory.
The proposer receives the full immutable work-breakdown analysis snapshot plus declared relevant context slices pinned to exact artifact versions, content digests, or repository commits.
WorkDependencyAnalysis exposes one analyze-dependencies operation that recomputes a complete candidate DAG from each exact full WorkBreakdownBaseline snapshot.
The module persists only the dependency DAG while downstream runtime state derives runnable frontiers.
V1 provides a native structured proposer, OPA policy evaluation, Graphology-DAG mechanics, a bounded Spec Kit consistency reviewer, and optional Task Master and OpenSpec proposal adapters.
A proposer proposes dependencies; trusted Core validates Graphology-DAG mechanics; OPA evaluates the exact policy bundle; WorkDependencyGate verifies semantic completeness and promotes.

dependencies: A bounded Spec Kit consistency-review binding plus optional Task Master and OpenSpec proposal bindings.
A durable host for artifact, checkpoint, graph, approval, and execution-record persistence.
A version-pinned OPA policy bundle and deterministic evaluation host.
Approved ProjectOverview, requirements, architecture, contract-disposition, and repository contracts.
Approved WorkBreakdown 0.1.0 and exact WorkBreakdownBaseline contract.
Bounded adapters or compatible implementations for configured module capabilities.
Explicit human or automated approval policy at configured gates.
Generic registry, effect checkpoint, Gate replay, and TraceabilityGraph boundaries.
Pinned Graphology and Graphology-DAG libraries behind the Core graph-mechanics boundary.
Versioned canonical contracts for each V1 module and lifecycle artifact.
risks: A consistency reviewer may be mistaken for authority unless reviewer findings remain advisory inputs to the Gate.
Adapter-native semantics may leak into canonical contracts unless conformance remains strict.
Ambiguous edge direction could duplicate inverse facts.
Analyzer silence could be mistaken for proof that no dependency is missing.
Conditional routing may become implicit unless every condition remains state-driven and evidence-bound.
Context slices may omit a semantically relevant source region unless Gate coverage checks remain independent of proposer selection.
Gate proliferation may add friction unless quick paths remain clear and policy is risk-adjusted.
Graphology traversal or serialization order may leak nondeterminism unless Core canonicalizes all externally visible artifacts and diagnostics.
Hidden adapter-selected context could violate deterministic invocation contracts.
Module boundaries may drift into duplicated responsibility unless every contract keeps one primary purpose.
OPA policy success may be mistaken for semantic completeness unless WorkDependencyGate separately reviews missing-dependency evidence.
Reused task adapters could blur decomposition and dependency authority.
Stored execution waves could couple static dependencies to changing runtime state.
Traceability may become incomplete when future contributors omit required lifecycle relationships or evidence horizons.
deliverables: A complete V1 module and gate contract inventory.
A deterministic provider-neutral orchestration kernel and host integration boundary.
A project-wide RequirementsBaseline, ProjectOverviewBaseline, and generated ProjectOverview.md.
Approved WorkDependencyAnalysis requirements and ProjectOverview baseline.
Bounded manifests, fixtures, dogfood evidence, release docs, and audit results.
Canonical artifacts, manifest, Gate, runtime contracts, and trusted contributor.
Executable conformance fixtures and verification evidence for every implemented lifecycle slice.
TraceabilityGraph coverage from business objectives through business acceptance.
Versioned bounded adapter manifests for replaceable external engineering capabilities.

reason: Define the approved WorkDependencyAnalysis module boundary, context-slice model, native proposal path, OPA policy evaluation, Graphology-DAG mechanics, consistency review, and optional proposal adapters.
risks: Version-pinned context slices can omit relevant context if Gate coverage review is weak.
Policy and graph-library success can be mistaken for semantic completeness.
Optional proposal tools can leak native semantics unless normalization remains strict.
